thread:
incident-bot: PAGER — geodns: elevated resolver timeouts from eu-west-1 probes (Route53 <> Cloudflare paths). Alerting on 25%+ DNS failures for customer-facing A/AAAA lookups for the last 5m.

oncall-alex: ack. grabbing context — which customers/paths?

taylor: seeing high 5xxs from auth-service behind eu-lb, looks correlated to DNS resolution failures (timeouts -> upstream retries -> 502s).

maria: confirmed: our internal probe fleet shows intermittent timeouts when querying Cloudflare resolver IPs from eu-west-1: `1.1.1.1` and some Route53 resolver addresses timing out.

jamal: any change window recently for geodns policy or Route53 health checks?

maria: no config rollouts in the last 6h. metrics show spike ~7067001100.

support-sophie: customers are reporting intermittent site failures and login issues, large SaaS customer X reported 30% of requests failing in EU for ~8m.

oncall-alex: ok, triage plan: 1) confirm scope via active dig from eu probes, 2) flip geodns fallback to prefer secondary resolver pool for eu while we investigate, 3) open vendor tickets with Cloudflare & AWS.

taylor: running quick checks now.

# quick checks (from eu-probe-12):
```
dig +time=3 @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai A +short || echo "timeout"
# -> timeout intermittently, 40% in last 10 queries

dig +time=3 @54.239.0.0 api.redwood.ai A +short || echo "timeout"
# Route53 outbound resolver (example) -> some responses but inconsistent TTLs
```

maria: adding traceroute to Cloudflare resolver IPs: packet loss ~20% between eu-azb -> peering point. Looks like upstream network flap.

jamal: I can flip fallback policy from the geodns control plane: switch eu region to prefer our secondary resolvers (internal-cached) with TTL=30s. Want me to proceed?

oncall-alex: Yes do it, add a canary first (10% traffic), monitor error rate for 5m.

jamal: applying canary now -> `geodns set-fallback --region eu --policy prefer-secondary --weight 10 --ttl 30`

taylor: monitoring application 5xx rate and DNS errors. Dashboards show immediate drop in DNS timeouts for canaried probes.

support-sophie: customer-impact update: major EU customers saw errors; on track to reduce with fallback. communicating to CS that mitigation started.

incident-bot: Deployment event: geodns fallback policy canary applied by jamal at 7067001255.

maria: reaching out to Cloudflare via support chat — they show no global incident but see elevated packet loss on specific peering edge. Raising to L2.

cf-status-bot: Cloudflare: No status page incident. Logged ticket CF-2026-7067 for assigned engineer.

oncall-alex: if vendor cannot confirm quick fix, we'll widen fallback to 100% and increase TTL to 60s to reduce churn. Thoughts?

taylor: widening to 100% if we see persistent >5% DNS errors after 10m. Also will enable extra resolver retries (client side) on our agents to tolerate transient failures: `RESOLVER_RETRIES=3` for probe fleet.

jamal: rolling to 100% now based on steady canary success. `geodns set-fallback --region eu --policy prefer-secondary --weight 100 --ttl 60` -> applied 7067001332.

incident-bot: Mitigation note: geodns fallback at 100% for eu applied. Monitoring.

maria: network team confirmed a peering flap between eu-isp-4 and cf-eu-edge causing selective drops. Cloudflare is coordinating with ISP.

support-sophie: notifying affected customers: "We are aware of intermittent DNS-related errors in EU. We have applied a temporary routing fallback and are actively working with providers. We'll update in 30 minutes."

oncall-alex: good. logging incident severity: SEV2 (partial customer impact, mitigation in place). Creating incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/7067001234

jamal: opening AWS support case for Route53 health check anomalies (case 12345678). attaching probe logs and dig traces.

cf-status-bot: Cloudflare engineer responded: investigating peering congestion at AMS PoP, may take 30-45 minutes to clear; recommended fallback + caching.

maria: continued monitoring: DNS error rate dropped from 25% -> 2% after full fallback. Application 5xx reduced by ~80% for EU traffic.

support-sophie: CS updated customers with the mitigation and ETA for vendor fix. No escalations to execs yet.

oncall-alex: plan for next steps: 1) keep fallback in place until vendors confirm peering healed, 2) collect packet captures and route analytics for postmortem, 3) add an automated playbook to detect and auto-failover this specific peering pattern, 4) follow-up postmortem in 48h.

taylor: noted action items, will open postmortem ticket and assign owners. Also propose increasing health-check frequency on critical resolvers during busy windows.

jamal: will revert TTL back to normal once vendors confirm stability.

incident-bot: Incident updated: SEV2 -> mitigation applied. Next update scheduled at +30m.

support-sophie: closing update for now; PS team queued a proactive outreach to top affected customers.

oncall-alex: thanks team — keep monitoring and post updates here.

# Action items (brief):
- jamal: keep fallback and revert after vendor confirmation (owner)
- maria: gather traceroutes + pcap and send to Cloudflare/AWS (owner)
- taylor: write postmortem skeleton and assign reviewers (owner)
- support-sophie: customer comms + maintain log of affected customers (owner)

oncall-alex: closing incident thread once vendors confirm full peering recovery.
